reason: The Hebrew text (Genesis 24) portrays regular people—specifically Abraham's elderly servant and Rebekah's family—in highly favorable terms. The servant is depicted as faithful, pious, wise, and honorable, earnestly praying to God (הַקְרֵה־ נָ֥א לְפָנַ֖י הַיּ֑וֹם) and acting with integrity. Rebekah is described as exceptionally beautiful (טֹבַ֤ת מַרְאֶה֙ מְאֹ֔ד), virtuous, and generous—willingly providing water to both the stranger and his camels. Her family members (Laban and Bethuel) are portrayed as hospitable and respectful of God's will (מֵיְהוָ֖ה יָצָ֣א הַדָּבָ֑ר). Throughout the narrative, these ordinary individuals demonstrate exemplary virtues of kindness, faithfulness, and piety.
